records.subject: Sorry to see you go
records.body:
Hi Mateo,

Cancellation confirmed. If there's anything we could've done differently, I'd appreciate hearing it -- always trying to get better.

Thanks,
Chidi Haddad

records.subject: Still want to get Orchard Partners set up on Wrenfield?
records.body:
Hi Mateo,

Checking back in on Orchard Partners -- if there's a reason setup hasn't happened yet, I'd like to understand it so we can fix it.

Chidi Haddad

records.subject: Anything I can help with?
records.body:
Hi Mateo,

Wanted to check in on Orchard Partners' setup. If you haven't gotten to inviting the rest of the team yet, no rush -- just let me know if anything's in the way.

Thanks,
Chidi Haddad

records.subject: Getting started with Wrenfield
records.body:
Hi Mateo,

Welcome! Wrenfield works best once there's a real project in it, so that's the one thing I'd suggest doing first. Inviting your team comes next -- tasks are a lot more useful once more than one person is on them.

Reply any time.

Thanks,
Chidi Haddad

decisions.rationale: Six days in with zero customer replies to three outreach emails (email:efd02569, email:4eb22fe9, email:e122183f), no project, no invite, no tickets — no signal of engagement at all. Starter plan, 8 days left. Unprompted self-activation after total silence is uncommon.

draft.subject: Getting Orchard Partners' first project started
draft.body:
Hi Mateo,

I know I've reached out a couple of times already, so I'll keep this short. Nothing is needed from you unless Wrenfield is still useful to Orchard Partners.

If it is, the one step that makes everything else click is a first project — projects are the main organizing unit, and tasks live inside them. The in-app onboarding flow walks through creating a first project, and a teammate can be invited from Account Settings -> Members at any time.

Would a 15-minute call this week help? I'm happy to work through that first project with you.

Best,
Chidi
